spec.name: softmax_qwen2_5_0p5b_a16
spec.description: Softmax sequencer over a row of at most 256 scores: max pass, exponential pass with sum, one reciprocal, normalising multiply

derivation.rule: capacity is one attention row tile; the score and weight formats come from the exponential unit and the normalising shift from the reciprocal, so a change to either changes this block

ports.name: n
ports.desc: number of scores in the row

ports.name: s_data
ports.desc: score, registered read, one cycle after s_addr

ports.name: w_valid
ports.desc: a normalised weight is on w_data

ports.name: w_index
ports.desc: which score the weight belongs to

behavior: start is a one-cycle pulse that begins a row of n scores, 1 <= n <= 256, held stable for the whole row. busy must be high on the clock edge that samples start, so it already reads 1 one cycle later, and it stays high until the last weight has been emitted.

Scores are read through s_addr and s_data, and the read is registered: s_data carries score[a] on the cycle after s_addr = a. If s_addr is itself a register, that is two clock edges after the edge that loads a into it: one edge updates s_addr and the next one reads the memory. Count those two edges when pairing each score with its index.
Pass 1 reads every score and keeps the maximum mx. The exponential is only defined for non-positive arguments, and subtracting the row maximum is what guarantees that.

Pass 2 feeds e_i = expu(d_i) for every i, where d_i = max(score_i - mx, -2**12): score_i - mx is never positive but can be far below the 13-bit signed input of expu, and below -2**12 the exponential is zero in its output format anyway, so the clamp is exact. Buffer every e_i, a 16-bit unsigned value, and accumulate their sum S. S is at most 256 * 2**15, so it fits the 24-bit input of recip without saturating.
S then goes through recip once, giving a mantissa m and a shift k. A divide per weight would be absurd.

Pass 3 emits, for every i, w_i = min(2**15, ((e_i << 15) * m) >> (40 - k)), with w_index = i and w_valid high for exactly that one cycle. The product is unsigned and needs about 48 bits; the min clamps any weight that would round above 1.0.
Weights may be emitted in any order, but each index exactly once per row, and w_valid must be low at every other time.

expu and recip are separate modules supplied as source files, not something to write. Instantiate them. expu has ports clk, rst_n, x (signed [12:0]), valid_in, y ([15:0]) and valid_out, with a latency of 3 cycles. recip has ports clk, rst_n, x ([23:0]), valid_in, y ([16:0], the mantissa m), k ([4:0], the shift) and valid_out, with a latency of 3 cycles. Use their valid_out rather than counting cycles.
All state resets to zero: busy and w_valid are 0 during reset.

timing.critical_path: from register _00000_ to register s1_full. This path takes longer than one clock period: add a pipeline register on it or split the logic between them.
